answer_1.quote: Recently, neural language generation (NLG) techniques based on encoder-decoder models, which are widely employed in machine translation and automatic summarization, have been applied to ad text generation (ATG).

answer_2.quote: To evaluate the generated texts quality, we employed two widely used metrics in ATG: BLEU-4 (B-4) and ROUGE-1 (R-1). These metrics assess the similarity between the generated text and reference based on n-gram overlap. Since paraphrases are commonly used in ad texts, BERTScore (BS), an embedding-based metric, was also used... Additionally, as task-specific guardrails, we introduce keyword insertion rates (KWD) and sentence length regulation compliance rates (REG).

answer_3.quote: To clarify the limitations and possibilities of automatic evaluation, we performed a meta-evaluation by adding a GPT-4 based evaluator to the set of the metrics used in the experiment in §5. The GPT-4 based evaluator was constructed by giving the same instructions as those given to the human raters in the manual evaluation §5.2.
methods: GPT-4 evaluator with same instructions as human evaluation

answer_4.quote: Three human raters who are native Japanese speakers with expertise in ad annotation evaluate each of the 10 ad texts of the 9 models and one original reference for each of the three evaluation aspects of faithfulness, fluency, and attractiveness.
answer_4.guideline: The evaluations were conducted: for faithfulness using absolute evaluation of whether the input document implies the ad text; for fluency using absolute evaluation of understandability and naturalness; and for attractiveness using pairwise comparison with human reference.
